title: PipelinePassCredential wire form
$comment: Structural residue of the credential.* rules (field presence, types, formats). Where a constraint is not expressible in JSON Schema, the $comment names the owning rule and its vectors. additionalProperties: true throughout is a schema-design consequence of credential.body-sot and credential.claim.open-world-accept (see those rules; not re-stated here).

@context.$comment: credential.field.context: W3C context first, dplaax protocol context present, profile extension contexts may follow. The protocol context URI is frozen as the v0 wire vocabulary; because @context rides the signing scope, repointing it is a cross-implementation hash partition — a next-MAJOR break.

issuer.$comment: credential.field.issuer: the Process DID. DID method is the wire profile's choice; controller-chain reconstructability is behavioral (not schema-checkable).

validFrom.$comment: credential.field.valid-from (vectors cred-006/007/030/031/032). format catches calendar-impossible values; the pattern pins the catalog residue: second precision, UTC only (Z or +00:00), no -00:00, and the canonical uppercase T/Z form (a schema-level wire-shape pin; the rule is silent on case).

credentialSubject.$comment: credential.field.subject: a single JSON object (arrays and scalars are excluded by type). outputHash presence is process-type-conditional (credential.subject.output-hash) and inputHash presence at a chain origin is issuance guidance (credential.subject.input-hash) — neither is wire-decidable, so both stay optional here with only the format pinned.

pipelineId.$comment: credential.subject.pipeline-id: format is the wire profile's choice.

processId.$comment: credential.subject.process-id: format is the wire profile's choice.

transformationClaim.$comment: credential.claim.grammar / credential.claim.bare-rejected: a single <namespace>:<label> value; a bare value (no namespace) fails the pattern. The charset classes (Unicode White_Space / Cc / Cf / '+', pinned to Unicode 15.0 by credential.claim.charset) are not portably expressible as a JSON Schema regex; cred-028/029 pin them.

inputHash.$comment: credential.subject.input-hash: format only; presence semantics are behavioral (chain.data-flow.continuity enforces presence on chain-preserving credentials via the continuity equality).

outputHash.$comment: credential.subject.output-hash: format only; the presence obligation is keyed to the process type (not wire-decidable).

previousCredential.$comment: credential.subject.previous-credential / credential.prev.content-hash: the proof-excluded canonical-body digest of the single predecessor. Omitted or null at a chain origin (receivers treat the two as equivalent). The pattern applies to the string form; null is the explicit-origin form.

id.$comment: credential.schema-ref: registry URI. The URI grammar is an open STATUS item (dplaax:schema/<name>@<version> is the reference implementation's canonical form); this schema deliberately does not pin it yet.

schema.$comment: credential.schema-ref: all three fields are needed once the object is present; absence of the whole object is acceptable.

derived_from.$comment: commitment.derived-from: a duplicate-free issuer DID set. The ascending lexicographic serialization order is not expressible in JSON Schema; commitment-003/004 pin it.

source_root.$comment: commitment.source-root.encode: multihash sha2-256 (0x12 0x20) in multibase lowercase hex (f prefix).

source_root_canonical.$comment: commitment.class.definition: names the canonical re-serialization for source_root leaves (e.g. jcs-rfc8785). An unknown identifier is a verification-time failed verdict (commitment.verify.equality-fail-closed), not a shape error.

proof.$comment: credential.field.proof / signer.proof.structure. type is deliberately NOT pinned to a literal: the owning rule requires W3C Data Integrity conformance without fixing the type value (contrast delegation.proof). See also credential.proof.as-received; created presence semantics: signer.proof.structure notes.
